![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040372/assets/89efcd0ecb51dac08a1102c5a347eea3459f7209de7cbac0a88b192259ca3b7e.png)

Consider the linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

What would be the image of the triangle shown above under the action of $\mathbf{T}?$
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ with associated $2 \times 2$ matrix $T,$ we have one of the following three possibilities:

- If $\mathbf{T}$ is non-singular, i.e., $\det(T) \neq 0,$ then the image of a two-dimensional object is a two-dimensional object. In particular, the image of a polygon with $n$ vertices is a polygon with $n$ vertices.

- If $\mathbf{T}$ is singular, i.e., $\det(T) = 0,$ we have two additional subcases:

- If $T$ has at least one nonzero entry, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a one-dimensional line segment.

- If $T$ is the zero matrix, then the image of a two-dimensional object is the point $(0,0),$ the origin of the coordinate system.

Since $T$ is the zero matrix, the image of our object under the action of $\mathbf{T}$ is the origin.

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following is the image of the triangle shown above under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the image of the triangle under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of the triangle:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the image's vertices are $(-2,2)$, $(-2,2),$ $(2,-2).$ Notice that all three points lie on the same line.

So, the image of our triangle under the action of $T$ is as follows:
